metadata.Name: PIQA
metadata.Description: This dataset focuses on physical commonsense reasoning, presenting multiple-choice questions about everyday physical interactions. It's designed to challenge language models by requiring them to understand how objects behave in the real world.
metadata.Paper Title: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language
metadata.Venue Name: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
Affiliations: Paul G. Allen School for Computer Science and Engineering, University of Washington
metadata.Abstract: To apply eyeshadow without a brush, should I use a cotton swab or a toothpick ? Questions requiring this kind of physical commonsense pose a challenge to today's natural language understanding systems. While recent pretrained models (such as BERT) have made progress on question answering over more abstract domains - such as news articles and encyclopedia entries, where text is plentiful - in more physical domains, text is inherently limited due to reporting bias. Can AI systems learn to reliably answer physical commonsense questions without experiencing the physical world?nnTo separate egg whites from the yolk using a water bottle, you should…nnIn this paper, we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA . Though humans find the dataset easy (95% accuracy), large pretrained models struggle ( ∼ 77%). We provide analysis about the dimensions of knowledge that existing models lack, which offers significant opportunities for future research.
